model.name: Reservation / Booking
model.purpose: Represent one governed request, hold and confirmation lifecycle for scarce or scheduled capacity so agents can understand what is sought, for whom, from which provider, under which terms, at what time and place, and with what operational evidence without confusing the reservation with inventory, contract, order, ticket, payment or fulfilment.
model.scope_statement: Owns reservation identity, versions, profiles and lifecycle; requester, booker, provider, beneficiary, broker, payer and contact bindings; reserved subject and external offering, inventory, availability and capacity references; segments, sub-reservations, units, quantities, party composition, preferences, accessibility needs, alternatives and dependencies; rate, price, tax, deposit, guarantee, cancellation, change, no-show and refund policy references; external offer, contract, order, ticket, entitlement, invoice and payment bindings; request, hold, waitlist, confirmation, modification, rebooking, split, merge, transfer, cancellation, expiry, no-show, correction and dispute assertions; desired, offered, held, confirmed, service, cancellation, check-in, fulfilment, observation and knowledge times; locations, routes, check-in and fulfilment evidence; provenance, privacy, retention, validation and loss-aware projections. External party, offering, inventory, contract, order, ticket, payment, schedule, location, fulfilment and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Reservation identity, versions, profiles, parties, reserved subject, availability and capacity references, composition, quantities, preferences and dependencies
Terms, guarantee and financial references, request, hold, confirmation, modification, cancellation, time, place, check-in and fulfilment evidence, governance, privacy, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Account, Offering, Product, Service, Resource, Inventory, Availability, Capacity Ledger, Schedule, Calendar Event, Location, Offer, Contract, Order, Ticket, Entitlement, Invoice, Payment, Check-in, Fulfilment or Records masters

Treating requested, held, confirmed, paid, ticketed, checked-in, fulfilled, cancelled or expired status as universal proof of legal validity, capacity allocation, attendance, service completion, refund or release
Autonomous scarce-capacity commitment, contract acceptance, charging, refunding, ticketing, transfer, cancellation, sensitive disclosure or physical record disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen parent agreement establishes obligations and legal terms. The reservation records capacity-seeking and booking lifecycle assertions and does not prove contract formation.
Availability is an observation and inventory systems own pools, quotas, units and allocation. The reservation stores source-qualified bindings and observed hold or release results.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Appointment, calendar event and reserved service
boundary_notes.distinction: An appointment or calendar event represents scheduled interaction and the service owns execution. The reservation owns booking intent, terms and confirmation bindings.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Offer, contract, order, ticket, entitlement, invoice and payment
boundary_notes.distinction: Each external commercial or fulfilment record has independent identity, state and authority; confirmation does not collapse or replace them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: UN/EDIFACT, Schema.org, IATA, TM Forum, EU law, RFC, PROV, ODRL, DQV, ISO 4217 and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has a distinct scope; every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.
